2:  * Line diff with unified output.
3:  *
4:  * Texts are compared line by line with a longest-common-subsequence walk;
5:  * output follows the unified diff format: two file headers, then one hunk per
6:  * changed region with up to `context` unchanged lines on each side.
7:  *
8:  * A line carries whether it ended with a newline, so the last line of a file
9:  * that does not end with one never matches the same text terminated normally.
10:  */
11: 
12: /** Marker printed after a line that is the end of a file without a newline. */
13: const NO_NEWLINE = '\\ No newline at end of file';
14: 
15: /**
16:  * Splits a text into lines and reports whether it ended with a newline.
17:  * @param {string} text Text to split.
18:  * @returns {{lines: string[], newlineAtEnd: boolean}} Lines without their terminators.
19:  * @throws {TypeError} When the text is not a string.
20:  */
21: export function splitLines(text) {
22:   if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new TypeError('text must be a string');
23:   if (text === '') return { lines: [], newlineAtEnd: true };
24:   const newlineAtEnd = text.endsWith('\n');
25:   const body = newlineAtEnd ? text.slice(0, -1) : text;
26:   return { lines: body.split('\n'), newlineAtEnd };
27: }

30:  * Turns a split text into tokens that remember their terminator.
31:  * @param {{lines: string[], newlineAtEnd: boolean}} split Result of `splitLines`.
32:  * @returns {Array<{text: string, terminated: boolean}>} One token per line.
33:  */
34: function tokenize(split) {
35:   return split.lines.map((text, index) => ({
36:     text,
37:     terminated: index < split.lines.length - 1 || split.newlineAtEnd,
38:   }));
39: }

41: /**
42:  * Builds the suffix table of longest-common-subsequence lengths.
43:  * @param {unknown[]} before Old items.
44:  * @param {unknown[]} after New items.
45:  * @param {(a: unknown, b: unknown) => boolean} same Item equality.
46:  * @returns {number[][]} Table where cell `i,j` is the LCS length of the suffixes.
47:  */
48: function lcsTable(before, after, same) {
49:   const rows = before.length;
50:   const columns = after.length;
51:   const table = Array.from({ length: rows + 1 }, () => new Array(columns + 1).fill(0));
52:   for (let i = rows - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
53:     for (let j = columns - 1; j >= 0; j -= 1) {
54:       table[i][j] = same(before[i], after[j])
55:         ? table[i + 1][j + 1] + 1
56:         : Math.max(table[i + 1][j], table[i][j + 1]);
57:     }
58:   }
59:   return table;
60: }

62: /**
63:  * Diffs two sequences.
64:  *
65:  * Where a deletion and an insertion are equally good, the deletion is emitted
66:  * first, so a replaced item reads as `-old` then `+new`.
67:  * @param {unknown[]} before Old items.
68:  * @param {unknown[]} after New items.
69:  * @param {(a: unknown, b: unknown) => boolean} same Item equality.
70:  * @returns {Array<{type: 'equal' | 'delete' | 'insert', item: unknown}>} Operations in file order.
71:  */
72: function diffSequence(before, after, same) {
73:   const table = lcsTable(before, after, same);
74:   const ops = [];
75:   let i = 0;
76:   let j = 0;
77:   while (i < before.length && j < after.length) {
78:     if (same(before[i], after[j])) {
79:       ops.push({ type: 'equal', item: before[i] });
80:       i += 1;
81:       j += 1;
82:     } else if (table[i + 1][j] > table[i][j + 1]) {
83:       ops.push({ type: 'delete', item: before[i] });
84:       i += 1;
85:     } else {
86:       ops.push({ type: 'insert', item: after[j] });
87:       j += 1;
88:     }
89:   }
90:   while (i < before.length) {
91:     ops.push({ type: 'delete', item: before[i] });
92:     i += 1;
93:   }
94:   while (j < after.length) {
95:     ops.push({ type: 'insert', item: after[j] });
96:     j += 1;
97:   }
98:   return ops;

101: /**
102:  * Diffs two line arrays, comparing line text alone.
103:  * @param {string[]} before Old lines.
104:  * @param {string[]} after New lines.
105:  * @returns {Array<{type: 'equal' | 'delete' | 'insert', line: string}>} Operations in file order.
106:  * @throws {TypeError} When either argument is not an array of strings.

116:  * @param {string} oldText Text before the change.
117:  * @param {string} newText Text after the change.
118:  * @returns {{added: number, removed: number, unchanged: number}} Line counts.
119:  */

121:   const ops = diffLines(splitLines(oldText).lines, splitLines(newText).lines);
122:   const stats = { added: 0, removed: 0, unchanged: 0 };

125:     else if (op.type === 'delete') stats.removed += 1;

137:  * @param {number} context Context lines on each side.
138:  * @returns {Array<{start: number, end: number}>} Inclusive operation ranges.
139:  */
140: function groupHunks(ops, context) {
141:   const changed = [];
142:   ops.forEach((op, index) => {
143:     if (op.type !== 'equal') changed.push(index);
144:   });
145:   if (changed.length === 0) return [];
146:   const runs = [];
147:   let start = changed[0];
148:   let end = changed[0];
149:   for (const index of changed.slice(1)) {
150:     if (index - end <= context * 2) {
151:       end = index;
152:     } else {
153:       runs.push([start, end]);
154:       start = index;
155:       end = index;
156:     }
157:   }
158:   runs.push([start, end]);
159:   return runs.map(([from, to]) => ({
160:     start: Math.max(0, from - context + 1),
161:     end: Math.min(ops.length - 1, to + context),
162:   }));

167:  * @param {number} start First line number, or the line before an empty range.
168:  * @param {number} count How many lines the hunk covers on this side.
169:  * @returns {string} Start and count, with the count omitted when it is one.
170:  */
171: function formatRange(start, count) {
172:   return count === 1 ? `${start}` : `${start},${count}`;
173: }

178:  * @param {string} newText Text after the change.
179:  * @param {{context?: number, oldName?: string, newName?: string}} [options] Rendering options.

193:   const hunks = groupHunks(ops, context);
194:   if (hunks.length === 0) return '';

196:   let oldNumber = 1;
197:   let newNumber = 1;
198:   const positions = ops.map((op) => {
199:     const at = { oldNumber, newNumber };
200:     if (op.type !== 'insert') oldNumber += 1;
201:     if (op.type !== 'delete') newNumber += 1;
202:     return at;
203:   });
204: 
205:   const out = [`--- ${oldName}`, `+++ ${newName}`];

207:     let oldCount = 0;
208:     let newCount = 0;

214:     const newStart = positions[hunk.start].newNumber;

238:  * @param {string} patch Unified diff produced by `unifiedDiff`.

`src/diff.js` renders a unified diff between two texts, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the defects. Keep the public exports, their signatures, and every behaviour the passing tests already pin; the module's own documentation states the intended contract, and the tests are fixed.

The module splits a text into lines, remembers whether the text ended with a newline, and compares the two line sequences with a longest-common-subsequence walk that prefers a deletion over an insertion when both are equally good. A line carries its terminator, so the last line of a text that does not end with a newline never matches the same text terminated normally; wherever such a line is printed, the marker `\ No newline at end of file` follows it, on whichever side of the diff it appears.

Output is the unified format: a `--- name` header, a `+++ name` header, then one hunk per changed region. A hunk shows up to `context` unchanged lines before and after the change, defaulting to three; two changed regions merge into a single hunk when at most `2 * context` unchanged lines separate them, since their context windows would otherwise touch. The hunk header reads `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@`, where a count of one is written without the comma and count, and a side that contributes no lines at all is written with a count of zero and the number of the line it follows — which is `0` at the start of a file. Identical texts produce an empty string, and any non-empty diff ends with a newline. `applyUnified` reverses the process, rebuilding the new text from the old text and the patch.
